title: WHO WERE THE ANAKIM?
paragraphs:
WHO WERE THE ANAKIM?
The Giants of Scripture, the Fear in Israel's Heart, and the God Who Turns Scandal Into Grace
There are names in Scripture that instantly awaken curiosity.
David.
Moses.
Paul.
Mary.
But then there are names that seem to emerge from the shadows of biblical history carrying mystery, fear, controversy, and unanswered questions.
One of those names is the Anakim.
Who were they?
Were they giants?
Were they human?
Why did entire nations tremble at the mention of them?
And why does their story still speak directly to the fears, insecurities, and spiritual battles we face today?
Because the story of the Anakim is not ultimately about giants.
It is about the terrifying moment when God's people looked at their problems and forgot how big their God was.
And if we're honest, many of us have done exactly the same thing.
The first time most readers encounter the Anakim is during Israel's approach to the Promised Land.
God had already delivered His people from Egypt.
He had parted the sea.
He had fed them in the wilderness.
He had provided water from rocks.
He had defeated enemies before them.
Yet when twelve spies entered Canaan and returned with their report, fear spread through the camp like wildfire.
Numbers 13:33 records their words:
"We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them."
The Hebrew text says:

וְשָׁם רָאִינוּ אֶת־הַנְּפִלִים
(v'sham ra'inu et-haNephilim)
"And there we saw the Nephilim..."
The spies continued by identifying the Anakim as descendants associated with the Nephilim tradition.
The word "Anakim" comes from עֲנָקִים ('Anaqim), descendants of Anak (עֲנָק, 'Anaq).
Scripture consistently describes them as unusually large and formidable people.
Deuteronomy 9:2 says:
"A people great and tall, the children of the Anakim, whom you know, and of whom you have heard it said, 'Who can stand before the children of Anak?'"
Notice something remarkable.
The problem wasn't simply the size of the Anakim.
The problem was the size of Israel's fear.
The spies did not merely report facts.
They interpreted reality through unbelief.
They saw giants and concluded defeat.
Joshua and Caleb saw the same giants and concluded victory because they trusted the Lord.
The difference was not eyesight.
It was faith.
Many people today live exactly like those ten fearful spies.
They look at debt and see a giant.
They look at addiction and see a giant.
They look at divorce and see a giant.
They look at depression and see a giant.
They look at their past and see a giant.
They look at their failures and see a giant.
And eventually they begin saying what Israel said:
"We are grasshoppers."
Fear has a way of shrinking people.
Sin has a way of shrinking people.
Shame has a way of shrinking people.
The enemy loves convincing believers that their giants are bigger than God's promises.
But Scripture never teaches us to measure our enemies.
Scripture teaches us to measure God.
The Anakim appear repeatedly throughout the Old Testament.
Joshua 11:21-22 records that Joshua eventually drove many of them from the land.
Yet some remained in places like Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
That detail becomes incredibly important later.
Because centuries afterward, another giant would emerge from Gath.
His name was Goliath.
The giant who terrified Israel's army likely came from the same giant-clan tradition associated with the Anakim and Rephaim.
Once again, Israel stood frozen in fear.
Once again, everyone focused on the giant.
Everyone except a shepherd boy who knew God.
David's perspective changed everything.
The soldiers saw a giant too big to kill.
David saw a giant too big to miss.
His confidence was not in his sling.
His confidence was in the covenant faithfulness of God.
When David confronted Goliath, he declared:
"You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts..."
(1 Samuel 17:45)
That is the heartbeat of the entire Anakim story.
Not giant strength.
God's strength.
Not human intimidation.
Divine faithfulness.
Not fear.
Faith.
Yet there is another layer to this story that often gets overlooked.
The Anakim remind us that God's people have always faced impossible situations.
Christianity has never been a faith designed for comfortable circumstances.
The Gospel itself emerged from what appeared to be defeat.
Think about it.
The disciples saw Jesus arrested.
The crowds mocked Him.
The religious leaders condemned Him.
The Roman Empire crucified Him.
To human eyes, Calvary looked like the victory of darkness.
But God was writing a different story.
The Greek word Jesus cried from the cross includes one of the most powerful declarations in history:

Τετέλεσται
(Tetelestai)
"It is finished."
Not defeated.
Finished.
Completed.
Accomplished.
The debt of sin paid in full.
The cross looked like a scandal.
It became grace.
The tomb looked like an ending.
It became a beginning.
The crucifixion looked like defeat.
It became redemption.
This is why our theme remains unchanged:
The Anakim teach us something profound.
The greatest giants are not always standing outside us.
Sometimes they live inside us.
Pride.
Unforgiveness.
Lust.
Bitterness.
Fear.
Self-condemnation.
Secret sin.
Those giants often appear larger than any army.
But Christ specializes in impossible victories.
The same God who led Joshua into Canaan.
The same God who empowered David against Goliath.
The same God who raised Jesus from the dead.
Is still working today.
Right now.
In your life.
In your marriage.
In your family.
In your ministry.
In your failures.
In your hidden wounds.
In your unanswered prayers.
The Gospel is not merely a message for people who have their lives together.
The Gospel is good news for people who know they don't.
That is why Jesus remains the true Giant Slayer.
Not because He destroys difficult circumstances immediately.
But because He conquers sin, death, hell, and everything that ultimately stands against God's purposes.
Maybe you have been staring at giants for so long that you have forgotten to look at Christ.
Maybe fear has become louder than faith.
Maybe shame has become louder than grace.
Maybe your past has become louder than God's promises.
Today, remember what Israel forgot.
The size of the giant never determines the outcome.
The size of God does.
And there is no giant larger than the resurrected King.
If this article strengthened your faith, don't let it stop with you.
Someone battling fear.
Someone carrying shame.
Someone who feels overwhelmed by life.
Someone who needs to know that God is still writing their story.
"Christ is bigger than my giants."
Or:
"I'm still fighting."
Or:
"Jesus rewrites everything."
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
One meaningful way to glorify God is by helping spread His truth to others.
Because one article can encourage a believer.
One share can reach a family.
One testimony can change a life.
And one Savior can change eternity.
The giants were never the end of the story.
Jesus always is.
